images.title: Punjab varies more than Kerala
images.purpose: Shows the two temperature lines on one grid with only the rise of each line marked, so the main reading stands out.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. One line graph filling the centre, two lines, and two vertical brackets on the right comparing how much each line rises.
images.exact_structure: Axes: 12 evenly spaced month ticks along the bottom, only the first labelled Jan and the last labelled Dec; vertical axis from 10 to 40 with 4 ticks at 10, 20, 30 and 40, only 10 and 40 labelled; faint grey horizontal grid lines at 20 and 30. Punjab line in vermilion (#D55E00) with 12 small square marks at about 19, 23, 28, 34, 37, 38, 34.5, 34, 34, 31, 27, 23. Kerala line in teal (#0072B2) with 12 small circle marks at about 31, 32, 32.5, 33, 32, 30, 29, 29.5, 30, 30.5, 31, 31. Each line has its name at its right end: Punjab and Kerala. To the right of the graph, a vermilion vertical bracket from 19 to 38 labelled rise about 19 degrees, and a short teal vertical bracket from 29 to 33 labelled rise about 4 degrees.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Punjab's line rises about 19 degrees in a year, Kerala's only about 4.
images.description: Shows the two temperature lines on one grid with only the rise of each line marked, so the main reading stands out.
images.context: Values approximate, read from the book graph: Punjab low about 19 in January, high 38 in June, about 23 in December; Kerala between about 29 (July) and 33 (April).
images.teaching_notes: Step one is the axes and marks, step two is the brackets.

image_decisions.why: Two lines with their yearly rise marked show the step two finding: Punjab varies much more than Kerala.
